title: Strong Password Checker II
summary: A password is considered strong if it meets eight criteria: it is at least 8 characters long, includes at least one lowercase letter, one uppercase letter, one digit, and one special character from a specified set.
statement: A password is considered strong if it meets eight criteria: it is at least 8 characters long, includes at least one lowercase letter, one uppercase letter, one digit, and one special character from a specified set. Additionally, no two identical characters can be adjacent. The function evaluates a given password string and returns true if it is strong, otherwise false.
constraints: A strong password has length at least eight and contains lowercase, uppercase, digit, and one of !@#$%^&*()-+.
No two adjacent characters may be identical.
Return true only when every condition holds.
hints: Evaluate each independent strength requirement directly.
Use any checks for the four character classes and pairwise comparison for adjacent duplicates.
Return the conjunction of length, lowercase, uppercase, digit, special, and adjacency predicates.
The conjunction is true exactly when none of the required conditions fails.
editorial: The conjunction is true exactly when none of the required conditions fails.

tests.explanation: The password is long enough, covers all four character classes, and has no repeated neighbors.
The adjacent two hyphens violate the no-identical-neighbors rule.
